newsitem.title: GERMANY: Employers see chance to end unions' sick-pay row.
newsitem.headline: Employers see chance to end unions' sick-pay row.

text.p: Werner Stumpfe, president of the Gesamtmetall metal and engineering employers federation, said on Wednesday he still saw a chance of resolving the sick-pay dispute in the sector.

Speaking after a board meeting of Gesamtmetall in Frankfurt he told a news briefing: "Negotiations have already been agreed in the regions for the 1997 wage round which are due to start early to mid-December."
"There are then still numerous opportunities to reach the urgently necessary solution of the conflict," Stumpfe said.
Stumpfe said the federation was still willing to consider any regional agreements on the issue as a possible pilot agreement for a nationwide agreement and regional deals.

Stumpfe's comments came only one day after efforts to reach such a pilot deal in North Rhine-Westphalia collapsed after a marathon negotiating session where both sides had been modestly optimistic that a deal could be reached.
In the end though, both sides said the sick-pay issue, where employers wish to abide by a law allowing them to cut back workers' salaries to 80 percent during illness, helped the talks collapse.
